availability.note: Historical completeness and current rank eligibility are distinct. Current ranks include every complete tracked model, including retired routes that keep their cached drafts on the board; models with an attested unavailable task retain an archived scorecard and are not compared against that field.

judge_note: Scores by 4-judge panel: Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort (Claude Code subscription) + GLM 5.3 Flash (OpenRouter) + GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning (Codex CLI) + Jev 1.13, typed judge (TypeSafe).

editorial_review.description: The reference scripts went through a collaborative editorial process by the Towards AI content/editorial team. This included review from 2 AI engineers, 1 professional writer, 2 YouTube/script-optimization reviewers with experience in YouTube content, and 1 fact reviewer with strong writing and editing expertise. A final editing pass was then completed by the Towards AI content lead. This was not a blind independent annotation setup, so no inter-rater reliability score is reported. Instead, the team worked collaboratively toward a final version that satisfied the editorial criteria. The reference scripts represent the resulting team-reviewed editorial standard.

bt_check.method: Bradley-Terry MLE (Hunter MM), ties = half win each, fit on the exact pairwise outcomes the published Elo uses — the same model + tie handling as LMArena's arena-rank. Deterministic: no shuffle passes, no K-factor. Ratings shown on the Elo scale, mean-matched to the published board.

elo.description: Elo is calculated from pairwise comparisons between model outputs on each task. Every output is scored once on the weighted rubric; then, for each task, every pair of models is compared and the one with the higher weighted overall score wins, with statistically-indistinguishable pairs counted as draws (the comparison uses each script's rubric score, not a separate side-by-side judgment). These outcomes are aggregated into an Elo-style relative ranking, averaged over many shuffled passes so update order doesn't bias the result. Elo should be read as a relative ranking signal within this benchmark, not an absolute universal quality score.
elo.draw_note: A pair is a draw when its overall gap on a task is within what the two cells' run-to-run noise can explain: |diff| ≤ t*·√(SE_a²+SE_b²), where SE uses the sample standard deviation over the cell's N run overalls and t* is the two-sided 95% Welch-Satterthwaite Student-t critical value for those two small samples, with a floor of 1.0 point. 'Draw' therefore means 'statistically indistinguishable on this task', not an arbitrary fixed band.
elo.formula_note: Elo updates use pairwise win/loss/draw outcomes and the expected-score difference between two systems (logistic, base 400); ratings start at 1500 with K=16, averaged over 25 seeds × 4 passes.

pairwise_check.note: Independent head-to-head check: the judge saw two anonymized scripts side by side (both orders; only order-consistent verdicts count as wins) and never saw the rubric scores. order_consistency is the share of pair-cells where the two order-swapped verdicts agreed. IMPORTANT framing: window-W pairing compares near-neighbours, i.e. mostly pairs whose bootstrap CIs overlap — near-ties the board itself does not claim to order. Low spearman/consistency over those pairs is expected sampling noise. settled_pair_agreement — head-to-head agreement on the pairs the board claims ARE settled (non-overlapping CIs) — is the statistic that could actually contradict the board.

draw_rule_validation.note: Every unordered current-model pair on every task is checked. The comparison shows exactly how many outcomes the N-aware Student-t rule changes relative to the former large-sample 1.96 shortcut.

separability.note: Fraction of model pairs whose bootstrap 95% Elo CIs do not overlap — the share of the board's ordering claims the data actually settles (Arena-Hard's 'separability with confidence'). Adjacent-pair separability is expected to be low everywhere (neighbours are near-ties by construction); the all-pairs number is the headline. Reference points: Arena-Hard 87.4%, MT-Bench 22.6%.

task_sensitivity.note: Each model's Elo rank recomputed with one task dropped from the arena, for every task. max_shift is the largest rank move any drop causes; small values mean the ranking does not hinge on a single topic. top1_stable is whether the headline #1 stays #1 under every drop.

elo.uncertainty_note: Each model carries a 95% confidence interval (elo_ci) from a bootstrap over the per-run scores: every (model, task) cell's N run overalls are resampled with replacement, the arena is rebuilt, and Elo is recomputed (200 repetitions). Overlapping intervals mean the ranking between those models is not settled.

analysis.note: inter_metric_residual is the halo indicator: correlation of the panel consensus's per-metric deviations across re-runs of the same model×task, with model quality subtracted out. length_bias_residual_r asks whether the judge panel scores the longer variant of the same model higher (length is scored deterministically and word counts are withheld from the judge; this audits what leaks through anyway). Cell-level numbers mix real quality correlation with halo and are context only.

judge.description: Each script gets one call from each of four judges: Claude Opus 5.5 at medium effort through the Claude Code subscription, GPT-6.1 Sol at medium reasoning through the Codex CLI, GLM 5.3 Flash through OpenRouter, and Jev 1.13 from TypeSafe. The three LLM judges use the identical fixed rubric prompt. Jev answers one question per metric in the same typed request by choosing among five described quality levels. The published score for each metric is the unweighted mean of the four judgments. No judge is fine-tuned. For each metric the three LLM judges must first quote short verbatim evidence from the candidate and only then score (halo mitigation); the quotes are stored with every run for auditability. Jev writes no text: it scores each metric as a separate question, and its per-level probabilities are stored instead, mapped onto the LLM judges' scale by a fixed per-metric calibration. No judge is told the script's word count; length is measured separately in code.

length_control.note: AlpacaEval-2-style length control: the panel-consensus length slope is estimated from within-cell variation only (same model, same brief, 5 samples), then every run's overall is counterfactually rescored at its task's cross-model mean spoken length and models re-ranked. beta_per_100_words is the estimated score change per +100 spoken words; a near-1 spearman and empty top15_shifts mean the published ranking does not ride on verbosity.

judge.model: 4-judge panel: Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort (Claude Code subscription) + GLM 5.3 Flash (OpenRouter) + GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning (Codex CLI) + Jev 1.13, typed judge (TypeSafe)

panel_scoring.aggregation: per-draft, per-metric unweighted mean across the 4 judges

published.label: Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort (Claude Code subscription)

panel_scoring.note: Every published score is the consensus of four judges scoring the same stored draft: three family-disjoint LLM judges using the identical rubric prompt, and Jev, a typed decision model from TypeSafe (no model on this board) that answers one described-level question per metric. No family judges its own models alone, so any single judge's family tilt is diluted by the three others.

judge.self_preference_note: Any LLM judge may slightly favor its own model family — stylistic affinity, not recognition, since judging is blind. We measured this directly under the earlier single-judge regime by re-judging the same outputs with different judges: every family scored itself highest, by different amounts. That measurement is why the published score is now a panel of three LLM judges from three different families (Anthropic, OpenAI, Z.ai/GLM) plus Jev, a typed judge from TypeSafe with no model on this board: each LLM judge's family tilt is diluted by the three judges that don't share it, and no family's models are scored by their own family alone.

methodology.limitations: This benchmark should be interpreted as directional rather than statistically definitive, especially while the reference set is small. It is designed to compare outputs against Towards AI's editorial criteria for educational video scripts, not to measure all possible dimensions of content performance.

reference_set.authorship: Reference scripts are AI-assisted and human-written by the Towards AI editorial team, with the final versions being mostly human-written and editorially refined. They represent the style and quality bar of Towards AI educational video scripts.

items.video_type: personal technical walkthrough / agentic workflow case study

reference_set.topics_note: The reference scripts' titles and video links are deliberately withheld to keep the benchmark hard to contaminate.

weights.rationale: The specific metric weights are domain-expert editorial weights chosen by the Towards AI team. They reflect how much importance our team gives each criterion for useful, watchable AI educational content. This benchmark is not designed to optimize only for CTR. CTR is heavily affected by title, thumbnail, audience, and distribution, while this benchmark focuses on script quality: clarity, usefulness, structure, tone, hook quality, retention potential, and whether the content brings value to the viewer. These weights are configurable and may evolve as more human feedback, retention data, or editorial evidence becomes available.

sensitivity.note: Ranks recomputed under random perturbations of the editorial metric weights (Dirichlet around the published weights). rank_p05..rank_p95 spans 90% of samples; a small range means the ranking does not hinge on the exact weight choices. top1_stable_share is how often the headline #1 stays #1.
sensitivity.relative_sd_note: concentration 100 ≈ ±30% relative sd on mid-sized weights

metrics.desc: How precisely it captures the reference's anti-hype conversational voice, first-person 'I was there / I use this' experience, running editorial reactions, and 'told not reported' register.
metrics.label: Tone & Voice Match

metrics.desc: Sentence rhythm, clarity, paragraph polish, read-aloud quality, and whether the script feels naturally written rather than awkward, stiff, or mechanically assembled.
metrics.label: Writing Craft & Clarity

metrics.desc: Technical depth, factual accuracy, source grounding against the brief/research/reference, and value density: every section should teach or advance something without padding.
metrics.label: Substance, Accuracy & Value

metrics.desc: Each paragraph causes the next; a felt emotional register in every section (no Wikipedia blocks); the viewer is transported, not informed. Every section must advance with new information; value-less repetition, restating earlier points in new words, and rehashing recap conclusions are penalized.
metrics.label: Continuity & Emotion

metrics.desc: Genuine (non-formulaic) subscribe CTA in the intro, real comment CTA + one forward-looking question at the end, open loop planted and resolved, re-engagement beats, correct intro line, never 'like and subscribe'. CTAs and beats must be genuinely bridged into the content, not a bolted-on checklist.
metrics.label: YouTube Best Practices

metrics.desc: Power of the opening 15-30 seconds: surprising / contradictory / second-person or personal-frustration hook, clear value promise, no generic intro.
metrics.label: Hook Strength

metrics.desc: Spoken word count vs the target the brief sets; overshooting is penalized about twice as hard as undershooting (land on the target or just under it).
metrics.label: Length Adherence

metrics.desc: Combined anti-slop: a 50/50 blend of the judged anti-slop (stock phrasing and structures, numbers reframed and pushed to [SHOW:]) and the computed EQ-Bench + our-rules lexical slop (sam-paech/slop-score pipeline + our banned-phrase scan). Spoken dashes are counted by code only: three are free, then each one takes 2 points off the computed part, up to 20. 100 = no slop.
metrics.label: Slop Score (EQ-Bench + ours)

metrics.desc: Presence and usefulness of inline [SHOW:] cues at every meaningful visual change; spoken text still reads cleanly without them.
metrics.label: Visual Cue Quality

provenance.judge_model: 4-judge panel: Claude Opus 5.5, medium effort (Claude Code subscription) + GLM 5.3 Flash (OpenRouter) + GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning (Codex CLI) + Jev 1.13, typed judge (TypeSafe)
provenance.note: Scores are comparable only within one (judge × rubric × weights × contract × skills) fingerprint. On any change, re-judge the whole board in one batch. For tracking a model over time, prefer `overall` (absolute) over Elo, which shifts as models are added.
